draft.title: Early warning systems
card: An early warning system gives people time to act before a hazard arrives. In Australia, the Bureau of Meteorology (BoM) and emergency services run these systems.
Forecasts
The BoM uses weather data to predict storms, cyclones and heavy rain. It issues warnings when dangerous weather is likely.
Flood gauges
These measure how high the water is in a river. Rising readings show that a flood may be coming.
Alerts and messages
Alert levels tell people how serious a threat is. Emergency services can also send phone messages to people in the area at risk.
draft.remember: Forecasts, gauges, alert levels and phone messages give people time to act.

a.q: Why do emergency services send a phone message when a flood is expected?
opts: To give people time to act before the water arrives
To stop the river from rising any further
To tell people how much rain fell last year
To measure the height of the river
a.why: An early warning system is about giving people time to act before a hazard arrives. A phone message cannot change the river or measure it. Measuring the height of the river is the job of a flood gauge.
a.clue: Think about what people need before a hazard arrives.

b.q: A flood gauge on a river near the town of Lismore shows the water level rising quickly. What is this most useful for?
opts: Warning that a flood may be coming
Predicting next month's weather
Showing how many people live nearby
Stopping the rain from falling
b.why: A flood gauge measures how high the river is, so quickly rising readings show a flood may be on the way. It does not predict weather weeks ahead. That is the job of forecasts, which use weather data rather than river height.
b.clue: A gauge measures water in the river, not weather in the sky.

a.best: To give people time to act before the water arrives

b.best: Warning that a flood may be coming

problems.detail: The clue ('what people need before a hazard arrives') echoes the right option's wording ('before the water arrives'), so a student can match words without knowing the idea.

a.q: Why do emergency services send a phone message when a flood is expected?
opts: To give people time to act before the flood arrives
To lower the river level so the town stays dry
To report how much rain fell in the area last year
To measure how high the water in the river is now
a.why: An early warning system gives people time to act before a hazard arrives, such as moving to higher ground. A phone message cannot change the river or report on past rain. Measuring the height of the river is the job of a flood gauge, not a message.
a.clue: Who reads the message, and what can they then do?

opts: Warning that a flood may be coming
Predicting next month's weather
Measuring how much rain has fallen
Telling people a cyclone is forming
b.why: A flood gauge measures how high the river is, so quickly rising readings show a flood may be on the way. It does not predict weather weeks ahead or spot cyclones. That is the job of forecasts, which use weather data rather than river height.
b.clue: A gauge measures water in the river, not weather in the sky.
